alisha: Heads-up: ran a quick onboarding sweep for glimmer-13b-quant with a lightweight speculative prefill (spec-window=16, dynamic-budget).
Command: 
```
./onboard_e2e.sh --model glimmer-13b-q --speculative prefill --spec-window 16 --spec-budget-dyn --quant ptq-8 --evalsets nquad,narrative-long
```
Initial win: median token latency -35%, aggregate throughput +2.1x, cost/tok ~-42% vs fp16 no-spec. But we see a small EM erosion on NQ (exact match -1.2%) and an uptick in false-positives flagged by our qual-checker on long narrative prompts.

peter: Nice perf. How reproducible? seeds / sample size?

alisha: 3 seeds, sample=2500 (NQ 1200, chat 800, longform 500). Logging: logits, topk traces, and full KV snapshots saved to s3.

raj: Can you isolate quantization vs speculative path? Also curious if the dynamic budget logic is overly aggressive on low-entropy prefixes.

alisha: Ran two controls: (A) ptq-8 without speculative, (B) fp16 with speculative. Control A matches fp16 baseline quality, so quant alone looks OK. Control B (fp16+spec) shows similar quality dip -> blame mostly on speculative heuristics.

yael: Any sign of distribution shift? compute KL between token dists for first 32 tokens?

alisha: Yes: mean KL(first32) rises with larger budgets. Numbers (avg over NQ):
- spec-static-8: KL=0.012
- spec-static-16: KL=0.028
- spec-dyn: KL=0.054
The KL correlates with EM drop.

peter: Do we have per-question diffs? are failures concentrated on multi-hop or ambiguous prompts?

alisha: Mostly multi-hop and disambiguation prompts where speculative prefills a plausible-but-wrong clarifier. Example attached in artifacts: prompt id 472b where model inserts "yes" continuation that steers the answer.

raj: Could KV merge timing cause stale attention? If speculative tokens are stitched before final KV normalization, scoring can be off. Any runtime flags for safe-merge?

alisha: We have safe-merge flag but it was off for perf. Re-running with safe-merge=true (adds small p95 overhead) to test.

ops-bot: deploy note: staging rollout glimmer-13b-q speculative patch at 2024-03-05T09:17Z.

yael: Idea: cheap verifier after speculative pass. run a fast causal-scoring pass on original prefix+candidate and reject candidates with score delta worse than threshold.

peter: That sounds similar to rerank, but cheaper since it's scoring-only. What's the cost?

alisha: Scoring pass adds ~20ms median, ~80ms p95. When combined with spec-dyn p95 still ~18% below no-spec baseline. On the bad NQ subset, verifier recovers ~70% of the EM loss.

yael: Worth adding ablation with verifier threshold sweep and measure TCO (tokens saved vs extra scoring cost).

raj: Also include deterministic decoding runs (temp=0, top-p=0) to separate stochastic sampling noise from pure scoring-induced divergence.

alisha: Done. Deterministic runs show smaller but present EM gap -> speculative algorithm alters argmax path in some examples.

peter: Add KL threshold gate in canary: if KL(first32)>0.04 OR EM drop >0.8% block.

alisha: I'll push detailed CSVs and per-example diffs to the eval ticket. Saved scripts: /mnt/runs/1778009999/run_glimmer_spec_sweep.sh artifacts: s3://redwood-staging/onboard/glimmer/1778009999.tar.gz

ops-bot: artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-staging/onboard/glimmer/1778009999.tar.gz :package:

yael: Let's plan a 20m sync to decide whether verifier should be default for longform/multi-hop routes.

peter: +1. Also document the KL->EM mapping so PMs understand tradeoffs.

alisha: Will do. Posting short summary in the ticket and tagging @product for visibility.
